items.en: China's Xi urges US and Russia to join forces to safeguard world peace
items.zh: 習近平籲美俄與中國攜手維護世界和平
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin to work together with China to safeguard world peace, Al Jazeera reported. The appeal came around a trilateral meeting between the three leaders, an unprecedented format that Beijing has presented as a vehicle for managing great-power friction rather than deepening it. Xi framed cooperation among the three states as a condition for global stability, a message aimed at least partly at audiences worried that rivalry between Washington, Moscow and Beijing is hardening into open confrontation.

items.en: 'Groundbreaking' Trump-Xi-Putin summit: Five key takeaways
items.zh: 川習普三邊峰會：五大重點整理
items.summary: Leaders hailed the unprecedented Trump-Xi-Putin meeting as historic, with discussions spanning nuclear risks to energy flows, according to Al Jazeera's summary of the summit. The piece distils five takeaways from a gathering that had no clear precedent in modern diplomacy, noting that the agenda ranged widely but produced more atmosphere than binding commitment. Analysts quoted in Al Jazeera's coverage said statements by Trump and Putin pulled attention away from the planned programme, leaving the practical results of the meeting harder to assess than its symbolism.

items.en: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.zh: 國際法院裁定緬甸對羅興亞人犯下種族滅絕
items.summary: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time the court has found that a state committed the crime, Al Jazeera reported. The decision follows years of proceedings over the military campaign that drove hundreds of thousands of Rohingya out of Rakhine State. Al Jazeera's explainer notes the ruling's weight for a community still largely living in exile, while also setting out the limits of what the court can enforce, since implementation depends on state cooperation rather than any power of the court itself.

items.en: Somalia expels UAE ambassador, accuses Abu Dhabi of violating sovereignty
items.zh: 索馬利亞驅逐阿聯大使，指控侵犯主權
items.summary: Somalia has expelled the United Arab Emirates ambassador, saying Abu Dhabi is interfering in its internal affairs with actions that amount to an open invasion, Al Jazeera reported. The expulsion marks a sharp deterioration in a relationship that has swung between cooperation and confrontation for years, shaped by competing interests in Somali ports, security training and influence over regional administrations. The language used by Mogadishu is unusually blunt for a diplomatic rupture, signalling that the dispute is about control of territory and security arrangements rather than protocol.

items.en: Mosque set on fire in Israel, politicians blame Netanyahu's 'incitement'
items.zh: 以色列清真寺遭縱火，議員批納坦雅胡煽動
items.summary: A mosque has been set on fire in Israel, with Knesset members calling the incident a hate crime and Hamas blaming Israeli settler gangs, according to Al Jazeera. Several politicians linked the attack to what they described as incitement by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, arguing that official rhetoric has created permission for violence against Palestinian citizens of Israel and their places of worship. The arson adds to a pattern of attacks on religious sites that rights groups have tracked for years, and that have rarely resulted in prosecutions.

items.en: Grand Theft Auto VI launches to rave reviews after 13-year wait
items.zh: GTA 6 上市獲壓倒性好評，等了 13 年
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI has launched to rave reviews after a 13-year wait, with critics calling it a masterpiece, spectacular and an astonishing American epic, Al Jazeera reported. The release is one of the largest commercial events the entertainment industry has seen, and Al Jazeera's companion piece argues it demonstrates the cultural and economic heft of video games at a moment when the industry has been struggling with mass layoffs. Economists cited by the outlet even estimated the launch could cost the US up to a billion dollars in lost productivity.

items.en: Waymo suspends driverless freeway rides across US after California ban
items.zh: 加州禁令後，Waymo 全美暫停無人高速載客
items.summary: Waymo has suspended driverless rides on freeways across the United States after a ban in California, Al Jazeera reported. Freeway operation is the hardest part of the robotaxi problem, because speeds leave almost no margin for a late or wrong decision, and it is also the part regulators scrutinise most closely. Pausing the service nationwide rather than only in California suggests the company would rather absorb the loss of its fastest routes than defend them case by case while the regulatory position in its most important market is unsettled.

items.en: NASA's Voyager 1 hits record one light-day distance, 50 years after launch
items.zh: 航海家 1 號飛抵一光日之外，創歷史紀錄
items.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth, a record for a human-made object, roughly 50 years after it was launched, Al Jazeera reported. A one-light-day separation means a radio signal now takes a full day to cross the gap in each direction, so every command and every reply is part of a two-day conversation. The spacecraft has long since left the heliosphere and continues to return data from interstellar space on a power budget that shrinks a little every year.

items.en: FIFA Under-17 World Cup 2026 gets under way in Qatar despite USA withdrawal
items.zh: U-17 世界盃卡達開踢，美國退賽
items.summary: The FIFA Under-17 World Cup has got under way in Qatar, with the Dominican Republic replacing the United States after the American team withdrew, Al Jazeera reported. The 25-day tournament features 48 teams, and FIFA has played down the security concerns cited around the US withdrawal. The expanded format gives far more federations a route into a global finals than the old 24-team field did, which makes the competition a useful early look at the next generation of players for countries that rarely reach senior tournaments.

items.en: Pakistan's footballers show India sportsmanship after SAFF final defeat
items.zh: 南亞盃決賽落敗，巴基斯坦列隊向印度致意
items.summary: Pakistan's football team formed a guard of honour for India after losing the SAFF Championship final 2-1 in Bangladesh, Al Jazeera reported. India had come from behind to win the regional title, and the gesture from the losing side drew attention precisely because fixtures between the two countries are usually framed by political tension rather than sportsmanship. For Pakistan, reaching the final at all marked a step forward for a programme that has spent years dealing with administrative disruption and limited international fixtures.

items.en: Cameron Bancroft claims entire Australian team knew about 'Sandpapergate'
items.zh: 班克羅夫特爆料：澳洲全隊都知道砂紙事件
items.summary: Cameron Bancroft has said the entire Australian cricket team knew about the sandpaper ball-tampering scandal, contradicting Pat Cummins and admitting he lied to protect Cricket Australia's investigation, Al Jazeera reported. The claim reopens a case that has shadowed Australian cricket since 2018 and that the board had treated as settled with a small number of sanctions. Cricket Australia has responded by offering to open a forum for players while ruling out a fresh inquiry, a position that keeps the matter out of formal proceedings.

items.en: South Korea cheating scandal: Are AI smart glasses a threat to exams?
items.zh: 韓國作弊風波：AI 智慧眼鏡威脅考試公平？
items.summary: Al Jazeera examines whether AI smart glasses threaten the integrity of examinations, following a cheating scandal in South Korea, a country whose university entrance test is treated as a national event. The explainer looks at how wearable devices that can read a page and answer silently collapse the assumptions behind traditional invigilation, which was designed to catch notes and phones rather than eyewear that looks ordinary. It also considers what detection would require, and the cost of turning every high-stakes exam hall into a search checkpoint.

items.en: Police charge crowds at Brussels student march
items.zh: 布魯塞爾學生遊行，警方驅散人群
items.summary: Thousands of students and teachers marched in Brussels against higher tuition fees, education reforms and funding cuts, and police charged the crowds, Al Jazeera reported. The protest is part of a wave of student action across Europe over the cost of higher education and shrinking public budgets, with similar demonstrations reported in Denmark and France. The confrontation in Brussels raised the political temperature of a dispute that has so far been fought mainly in consultation rooms and parliamentary committees rather than on the street.

items.en: Young French students who see 'no change' keep up protests in Paris suburbs
items.zh: 看不到改變，巴黎郊區學生持續抗爭
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports from the Paris suburbs on young French students who say they see no change in their schools and are refusing to give up their protests. The piece traces the origin of France's education protests to conditions in under-resourced schools outside the capital, where students describe overcrowded classes, unfilled teaching posts and a sense that national debate rarely reaches them. Their persistence after the initial wave of demonstrations faded is what makes the movement harder for officials to treat as a passing disturbance.

items.en: Anthropic raises $81.3bn in biggest IPO of all time
items.zh: Anthropic 募資 813 億美元，史上最大 IPO
items.summary: Anthropic has raised 81.3 billion dollars in the largest initial public offering on record, pricing shares at 83 dollars in a blockbuster market debut that surpassed SpaceX, Al Jazeera reported. The AI company began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. Taiwanese market coverage put the first-day path at an open near 111.50 dollars and a close of 97.17 dollars, still well above the offer price but far below the opening print, which left the listing being read as a test of how much investors will pay for AI exposure.

items.en: US lawmakers launch probe into Lutnick's actions amid Nvidia scandal
items.zh: 美議員調查商務部長涉輝達案作為
items.summary: US lawmakers have launched an inquiry into Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's actions in connection with an Nvidia-related scandal, Al Jazeera reported. A letter from legislators alleges a possible conflict of interest in the secretary's decision not to add the firm Megaspeed to the US trade blacklist. The dispute sits at the centre of export-control policy for advanced chips, where listing decisions determine which buyers can legally obtain high-end accelerators, and where the line between commercial lobbying and national-security judgement is contested.

items.en: Can Anthropic afford to put AI safety first?
items.zh: 上市之後，Anthropic 還能把安全放第一？
items.summary: As Anthropic goes public, Al Jazeera asks whether the company can balance its safety promises against the pressure to keep investors happy. The question matters beyond one firm, because Anthropic has built its public identity on the claim that caution and commercial success are compatible, and a listing exposes that claim to quarterly scrutiny for the first time. The segment notes that public markets reward growth and shipping speed, which is exactly the trade-off that safety-focused research has historically been positioned against.

items.en: Kenshi Yonezu announces '2026 TOUR / GHOST' arena tour across six cities
items.zh: 米津玄師宣布 2026 巡演 GHOST，六城 14 場
items.summary: Kenshi Yonezu has announced a domestic arena tour titled 2026 TOUR / GHOST, with 14 shows across six cities including Nagano, Osaka, Aichi, Fukuoka, Miyagi and Kanagawa, Japanese music outlet Natalie reported. Priority ticket serial numbers were included with his 15th single, the usual route for Japanese arena tours where the earliest ballot is tied to a physical release. For fans outside Japan the practical point is that the first ballot runs through the single, so the CD purchase window matters as much as the ticket date.

items.en: Kenshi Yonezu to embark on largest-ever world tour spanning 11 cities
items.zh: 米津玄師啟動生涯最大規模世界巡演，共 11 城
items.summary: Kenshi Yonezu is heading out on the largest world tour of his career, taking in 11 cities in total including five he has never played before, according to Japanese music outlet Natalie. The expansion matters for Asian fans because adding new cities is how Japanese artists test demand outside the established Tokyo-Seoul-Taipei circuit, and a first-time stop usually means a smaller room and a harder ballot. Dates and ticketing for individual cities are announced separately, so watching the official schedule page is the only reliable route.

items.en: YOASOBI to play two nights at the Taipei Dome in January 2027
items.zh: YOASOBI 2027 年 1 月台北大巨蛋連唱兩天
items.summary: YOASOBI will perform two consecutive nights at the Taipei Dome in January 2027, with Taiwanese outlet Business Weekly reporting ticket pricing, the real-name registration requirement and the ballot-based sale process for the shows. The Taipei Dome booking is a step up in venue size for the duo in Taiwan, which is why the sale runs as a registered ballot rather than a straight on-sale. Anyone planning to go should note that real-name rules mean the ticket holder's identity is checked at entry.

items.en: Mrs. GREEN APPLE announce sixth album and first arena tour in three years
items.zh: Mrs. GREEN APPLE 宣布第六張專輯與三年來首度巡迴
items.summary: Mrs. GREEN APPLE have set a release date for their sixth album and announced their first arena tour in three years, Tokyohive reported. The band's official schedule page is where individual dates and any overseas legs appear first, and their fan club handles the earliest ballot. For listeners in Taiwan and Hong Kong, the pattern with this band has been that Asian dates, when they come, are confirmed well after the Japanese run, so the album cycle is the signal worth tracking rather than the tour announcement alone.

items.en: Yuuri to headline a Hong Kong concert at AsiaWorld-Expo
items.zh: 優里香港亞洲國際博覽館開唱
items.summary: Yuuri is scheduled to perform in Hong Kong at AsiaWorld-Expo, according to the venue's own upcoming-events listing. AsiaWorld-Expo is the larger of the two rooms Japanese acts normally use in Hong Kong, so the booking points to a full-scale production rather than a club date. The venue page is the authoritative source for the date and the on-sale, since Hong Kong shows for Japanese artists are often announced locally before anything appears on the artist's Japanese schedule page.
